title: Add MIT License to the project
feat: add GitHub Action wrapper for with-workbench
description:
## Summary

Adds `action.yml` so `with-workbench` can be used as a composite GitHub Action:

```yaml
- uses: posit-dev/with-workbench@main
  with:
    license-key: ${{ secrets.WORKBENCH_LICENSE }}
    version: "2026.01.1"
```

This mirrors the pattern established by `posit-dev/with-connect`, which already has an `action.yml`.

### Why

The CLI tool requires `uv tool install git+https://github.com/posit-dev/with-workbench.git`, which fails in GitHub Actions because the repo is internal — the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` can't clone it. As a composite action (`uses:`), GitHub handles the checkout natively with org-level access.

### Inputs/Outputs

**Inputs:** `license-key`, `version`, `image`, `port`, `user`, `password`, `quiet`, `stop`

**Outputs:** `WORKBENCH_URL`, `WORKBENCH_USER`, `WORKBENCH_PASSWORD`, `CONTAINER_ID`

### Usage

```yaml
- name: Start Workbench
  id: workbench
  uses: posit-dev/with-workbench@main
  with:
    license-key: ${{ secrets.WORKBENCH_LICENSE }}
    version: "2026.01.1"
    user: testuser
    password: "TestPass123!"

- name: Stop Workbench
  if: always()
  uses: posit-dev/with-workbench@main
  with:
    stop: ${{ steps.workbench.outputs.CONTAINER_ID }}
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify action works in a consuming workflow (posit-dev/vip has a companion PR)

title: fix: fail loudly when an image pull breaks mid-stream
description:
### What

`pull_image()` reported success for pulls that had actually failed.

The Docker daemon reports a mid-pull failure as an `error` chunk in the *body* of the `/images/create` stream, not as an HTTP error status. `client.api.pull()` calls `_raise_for_status` on the initial response only, before streaming begins, so it has already returned successfully by the time the pull breaks. Our loop inspected chunks solely for `Pull complete` / `Already exists`, so the error chunk fell through and `Successfully pulled <image>` printed unconditionally.

### Why it matters

Seen in [rstudio-pro run 33187667267](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/actions/runs/33187667267), preview leg:

```
15:58:12  Pulling image rstudio/rstudio-workbench-preview:jammy-daily...
16:00:33  Successfully pulled rstudio/rstudio-workbench-preview:jammy-daily
16:00:33  Starting Workbench container...
16:02:56  docker.errors.ImageNotFound: 404 ... No such image: rstudio/rstudio-workbench-preview:jammy-daily
```

Three separate costs:

1. The success message is a lie, and the real failure surfaces 2m23s later as `No such image` — pointing at the wrong component entirely.
2. `docker-py`'s own `images.pull()` has the same blind spot, so `containers.run()`'s automatic re-pull failed identically instead of reporting why. That re-pull is the 2m23s gap.
3. Because `pull_image()` never raised, `ensure_image()`'s fallback chain (preview registry, then local cache) was unreachable for this entire class of failure.

### Approach

Check each chunk for `error` and raise `docker.errors.APIError` with the registry's own reason, matching how `docker-py` itself handles stream errors in `models/images.py` (`if 'error' in chunk: raise ...`). `ensure_image()`'s existing `except Exception` then composes it, so the fallbacks work again and the operator sees the cause:

```
Failed to pull image: rstudio/rstudio-workbench:jammy: toomanyrequests: You have reached your pull rate limit
```

### Tests

`pull_image()` and `ensure_image()` had no coverage at all. Adds four cases: a stream error raises; a clean stream still succeeds; a failed pull with no cached image surfaces the registry reason; a failed pull with a cached image falls back to it. Full suite green via `uv run test_main.py`.

### Not addressed

This makes the failure honest, it does not make it rarer — a transient registry blip will still fail the run, now with a one-line reason. A bounded retry is a separate concern and deliberately not bundled here.

title: feat: use posit/workbench images for 2025.09 and later
description:
## Summary

Workbench releases are now published as `posit/workbench:<version>`, continuously since 2025.09.0. `rstudio/rstudio-workbench:jammy-<version>` remains for older releases.

| `--version` | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `release` / `latest` | `rstudio/rstudio-workbench:jammy` | `posit/workbench:latest` |
| `2025.09.0` and later | `rstudio/rstudio-workbench:jammy-<v>` | `posit/workbench:<v>` |
| older, or not a version number | `rstudio/rstudio-workbench:jammy-<v>` | unchanged |
| `preview` | `rstudio/rstudio-workbench-preview:jammy-daily` | unchanged |

The preview-registry fallback now applies to both image names. The `linux/amd64` pin is unchanged. `posit/workbench` is multi-arch, so dropping the pin for it would let arm64 runners run natively, but I've left that for a separate change.

## Testing

- Updated mapping tests, plus new tests for legacy and non-numeric versions (registered in the `__main__` runner).
- Live: `--version 2026.10.0` resolves to `posit/workbench:2026.10.0` and starts normally.

title: feat: add --api-token to enable the Workbench API and mint an API token
description:
## Summary

Adds an opt-in `--api-token <user|admin|super-admin>` (Action input `api-token`) for testing against the Workbench API. The motivating use case is [posit-sdk](https://github.com/posit-dev/posit-sdk-py)'s Bearer-token `posit.workbench.admin.Client`.

With `--api-token`, the tool:

- **Enables the API:** sets `workbench-api-enabled`, `workbench-api-admin-enabled` and `workbench-api-super-admin-enabled` in `rserver.conf`. Without them, rserver rejects Bearer tokens ("workbench-api-admin-enabled=1 missing in rserver.conf").
- **Enables audited jobs:** sets `audited-jobs=1`, without which `launch_audited_job` fails with "Audited jobs is not enabled".
- **Configures a SQLite audit database:** `get_historical_session` fails with "Audit DB must be initialized" otherwise.
- **Registers the user:** adds `--user` to Workbench's user database with `rstudio-server add-user`, as an admin for `admin`/`super-admin` tokens. Tokens can only be minted for registered users.
- **Mints the token:** runs `rstudio-server generate-api-token <type> with-workbench <user> --token-env …`. The token value is generated by the tool and passed through the environment, so it never appears in process arguments or output.
- **Verifies and outputs it:** checks the token against `/api/version` and outputs `WORKBENCH_API_KEY` and `WORKBENCH_VERSION`. It also passes `WORKBENCH_API_KEY` to commands run with `--`. In the Action, the key is masked.

The config is written into the *created but not yet started* container (`get_archive`/`put_archive`), so it works with any image and rserver never needs a restart. This is why `containers.run()` became `create()` + `start()`. Without `--api-token`, behaviour is unchanged.

## Testing

- **Unit tests:**
  - argument parsing;
  - the config rewrite (checked by unpacking the archive written to the container);
  - add-user and token commands, including that the token isn't in the args;
  - an existing-user case and a failure case;
  - version lookup and a rejected-token case;
  - `WORKBENCH_API_KEY` reaching the command environment.
  - Registered in the `__main__` runner.
- **CI:** a `test-action-api-token` job calls `get_historical_session` with the minted token.
- **Live:** with `posit/workbench:2026.10.0`, posit-sdk-py's Workbench integration suite (19 tests: jobs, audited jobs, sessions, users, compute environments) passes against a container started with `--api-token admin`.

Note: this and #4 (license deactivation) append tests in the same places in `test_main.py`, so whichever merges second needs a trivial rebase.

title: fix: deactivate the license before stopping and redact it from logs
description:
## Summary

Two fixes for running the tool in CI:

- **Deactivate the license before stopping.** The image deactivates the license in an `EXIT` trap of `startup.sh`, but that script runs `rserver` as a foreground child under supervisord. On `docker stop`, bash defers the trap until `rserver` exits, and supervisord kills everything after its stop timeout. So the trap usually never runs, and every run leaks a license activation. `stop_container()` now runs `license-manager deactivate` via `docker exec` before `container.stop()`, both in command mode and with `--stop`. A failed deactivation only prints a warning; the container is still stopped.
- **Redact the license key from printed logs.** On startup failure the tool prints the container logs. The image logs the `license-manager activate` result as JSON, including `"product-key": "<the key>"`, so the key ended up in the terminal or CI job logs. Logs (and the deactivation warning) are now redacted: the `product-key` field and any occurrence of the key itself.

## Testing

- New unit tests cover:
  - redaction of the `product-key` field and of the raw key;
  - deactivation happening before `stop`;
  - no deactivation when the container isn't running;
  - stopping still happening after a failed deactivation.
  - They're registered in the `__main__` runner, and `uv run test_main.py` and pytest both pass.
- Live check with `posit/workbench:2026.10.0`: start-only mode, then `--stop`. `license-manager deactivate` exited 0 and the container stopped.

Note: this and #5 (`--api-token`) append tests in the same places in `test_main.py`, so whichever merges second needs a trivial rebase.
